messages: maria (design): dropping the new mock for the Deployments > Rollouts panel here — focus is on the rollback confirmation microflow and the timeline condense state. https://redwood.design/app/rollouts/frames sam (eng): nice, saw the GIF. question: does the rollback modal block keyboard users? hard to tell from the clip. maria (design): good call — keyboard focus should land on the primary action ('Confirm rollback') and ESC should cancel. open to copy tweak suggestions. jonah (product): can we make the copy explicit about impact? current: "Confirm rollback" -> maybe "Confirm rollback to v1.3 — this will route 100% traffic to v1.3" tia (a11y): +1 to explicit copy. also need aria-live for status updates while rollback runs. screen readers should hear progress: "Rollback started", "Rollback 60%" etc. arjun (frontend): implementation notes: we can reuse the existing status bar component and add role="status" + aria-live="polite". also need focus trap in modal and restore focus to the timeline item after close. sam (eng): timeline restore focus sounds right. tricky bit: when we auto-collapse the timeline (condensed view) keyboard users still need to reach version details — propose a "Show versions" button with aria-expanded. maria (design): agreed. the condensed timeline has little affordance for keyboard so I'll add a visible "Show versions" control and an expanded/collapsed label. tia (a11y): color contrast on the canary traffic badge is low on the pink variant. use WCAG AA 4.5:1 for normal text. Also ensure the traffic slider has keyboard increments and a visually hidden label for the value. maria (design): good catch, I'll update swatches. For the slider aria, thinking: aria-label="canary traffic percentage" aria-valuemin="0" aria-valuemax="100" aria-valuenow="10" and arrow keys adjust by 5. any concerns? arjun (frontend): that's straightforward. but on small screens the tooltip showing % might cover other UI; we should avoid hover-only tooltips. use persistent visible text or on-focus tooltip. jonah (product): one more UX ask — when saving an A/B test variant split, we should show an inline confirmation with a small undo action (5s toast) instead of a full modal. lower friction. maria (design): nice. toast with "Undo" fits. we'll keep modal for destructive rollbacks and critical permission checks. sam (eng): permission gating: users without rollback perms should see the modal disabled with explanatory copy and a link to request access. we can wire that to the roles API. tia (a11y): confirm that disabled controls still expose reason text to screen readers. some JS frameworks hide it. arjun (frontend): noted. we will keep the reason in the DOM and connect it with aria-describedby. maria (design): small copy proposals for rollback modal: header: "Confirm rollback"; body: "Rolling back will revert live traffic to version v{X}. This may affect sessions and cached responses. Are you sure?" primary CTA: "Rollback to v{X}" secondary: "Cancel". any phrasing tweaks? jonah (product): maybe swap body to start with impact: "This will route 100% of live traffic to v{X} and invalidate some session state." then the ask. clearer for ops. tia (a11y): language is good. prefer "route" vs "revert"? both fine. ensure we don't use color-only cues for the severity. add an icon and role="alertdialog" for the modal. maria (design): will update comps and add a keyboard-only walkthrough GIF for accessibility review. deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for app-redwood @ 10% -> 1769456200 sam (eng): lol perfect timing, test case incoming. i'll prototype the focus trap and aria-live updates on the branch. maria (design): thanks all — i'll post updated frames by EOD and pingtia for a quick pass. :sparkles:
